builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
summary: SinkState replaces dense storage and full per-step rewriting of linear-attention recurrent states with an adaptive low-rank representation using buffered updates, top-subspace local SVD, and asynchronous CPU consolidation. It adds implementation complexity in the inference path: custom state management, rank adaptation logic, and CPU-offload synchronization beyond standard Mamba-SSM or FLA kernels. It can fail if a deployment's layers do not exhibit the assumed low-rank query/key/value concentration, if per-state rank variation makes the adaptive scheme unstable, or if CPU consolidation bandwidth becomes a bottleneck at high batch sizes.
rationale: The gains are meaningful and validated on 4B–120B models, but the technique only applies if the reader serves hybrid Mamba-2 or Gated DeltaNet models and is willing to integrate a nonstandard state-management layer, so it warrants a targeted pilot rather than immediate adoption.
technique: Adaptive low-rank SVD compression of recurrent states

claims.statement: SinkState replaces dense storage and full per-step rewriting of linear-attention recurrent states with an adaptive low-rank representation using buffered updates, top-subspace local SVD, and asynchronous CPU consolidation. It adds implementation complexity in the inference path: custom state management, rank adaptation logic, and CPU-offload synchronization beyond standard Mamba-SSM or FLA kernels. It can fail if a deployment's layers do not exhibit the assumed low-rank query/key/value concentration, if per-state rank variation makes the adaptive scheme unstable, or if CPU consolidation bandwidth becomes a bottleneck at high batch sizes.

Reduces peak recurrent-state memory by up to 2.6x (1.9x average) and speeds up decoding by up to 1.58x (1.25x average) over Mamba-SSM and FLA across four hybrid 4B–120B models, with accuracy maintained.
